newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX index surges to record closing high.
newsitem.headline: German DAX index surges to record closing high.

text.p: Germany's blue-chip DAX index rallied to end bourse trade at a new all-time closing high on Monday, with sentiment cheered by Wall Street's strong gains on Friday and the dollar's ongoing resilience at higher levels.

The 30-share DAX comfortably exceeded a previous record high of 3,474.28 points to end bourse up 68.41 points, or nearly two percent at 3,528.78 points, just off an all-time high of 3,533.18 points reached earlier in the session.
Part of the strong advance was a simple catch-up from Friday afternoon, when prices advanced strongly in the late post-bourse session following the release of well-received U.S. economic data.

"Things are fairly much booming," said a Frankfurt dealer. However, trading volumes were capped by a bank holiday in Britian and traders said the duration of the rally would depend on how U.S. financial markets performed later on.
"After the massive jump in the first quarter, people seemed to be a bit nervous and April seemed to be a bit of a consolidation phase," another trader said.
"If we don't get any massive dirt from the U.S. this may be sustainable," he said.
Dollar-sensitive car shares led the advance.

Volkswagen AG ended up over 3.5 percent at 1198 marks, off an earlier all-time high of 1,210 marks. The share registered little reaction to an announcement that VW's first quarter 1997 pre-tax profits were up 44 percent at 586 million marks.
Daimler-Benz AG ended nearly 3.5 percent higher at 136.20 marks, off an earlier high of 137.05 marks.
Financial shares also surged over the session. Index heavyweight Allianz AG Holding ended up 3.4 percent at 345.50 marks.
Dresdner Bank ended up 3.25 percent at 57.80 marks. Dealers said Germany's second-largest commercial bank was in a good technical position.

The underperformer of the day was software company SAP AG, whose DAX-listed preferred stock fell initially after Frankfurt prosecutors said they were probing a potentially serious insider trading case involving the company.
Dealers downplayed the move, noting that SAP is notoriously volatile and the share recovered over the bourse session to end up 3.10 marks at 324.50 marks.
"This (the story) is mainly a negative from a sentiment point of view," said a dealer. "It makes no difference to fundamentals."

Chemicals giant Hoechst was also under pressure over the pressure and ended the session down 1.30 marks at 66.35 marks, after reporting first-quarter pretax profit of 831 million marks, slightly below many estimated, according to dealers.

"Overall the numbers were slightly disappointing," said Christian Faitz, chemicals analyst at Trinkaus Capital Management, who noted that the data had been hard to predict because of Hoechst's current phase of restructuring.
